input.command: git status && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git log -5 --oneline && git status -u --ignored && ls -la artifacts scratch 2>/dev/null; node -e "console.log('tz', Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, 'offset', new Date().getTimezoneOffset())"
git remote -v && git log --oneline -3 && git branch -vv && git rev-parse HEAD origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null; git show-ref | head -50

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision>
Merchant calendar month via the request timezone, every row placed by `at` (refunds in the issued month), and net = gross - fees - refunds so the four figures foot to cash collected. Set aside UTC month buckets, the old sale-month refund rule, and net = gross - refunds with fees left out of the bottom line.
</decision>
<risk>
The net formula is the judgment call a reviewer should challenge. Zone-less datetimes are forced to UTC, and a date-only `at` is UTC midnight, so it can land in the previous local month west of UTC. An unknown timezone or unparseable timestamp throws.
</risk>
<verified>
`node scratch/check.ts` (New York winter and summer boundaries, Tokyo, Chatham +13:45, refund issue month vs sale month, negative net, duplicate ids) and `node smoke.ts` (module loads; the neutral fixture does not match the arguments).
</verified>
EOF
git add impl.ts artifacts && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git push -u origin HEAD && git status
